body.statement: Using the experiment-comparison handle, characterize a primitive necessary and sufficient condition for \(\mathfrak L_\alpha^\star<\mathfrak L_\alpha^{\mathrm{cc}}\) in general continuous outcome-adaptive platform designs, or prove that no criterion depending only on \((\Gamma,p_{\mathrm{floor}},\alpha,S)\) can be necessary and sufficient by constructing two admissible designs with the same four scalars and opposite strict-gain status. The characterization must compare the unrestricted full-record and concurrent-record interval kernels and must retain the information carried by realized propensity vectors.
body.justification: AIPW KKT improvement is neither necessary nor sufficient for strict gain among all honest interval kernels.
body.gap: Santacatterina et al. compare influence functions and the parent compares AIPW objectives; neither supplies an intrinsic comparison of the two observed-data experiments.
body.consumer: A regulator or trial designer needs to know whether nonconcurrent outcomes improve the best honest procedure, not merely whether they reduce one estimator's variance proxy.
